results.summary_before: This Wokwi project is a customizable UART transmitter that can send multiple ASCII characters by storing each character in a column of flip-flops. The characters can be modified by changing the multiplexer inputs to VCC or GND, and additional characters can be added by copying and pasting columns. Testing involves setting the baud rate to 300, toggling switches for load/transmit and output enable, and observing the serial output in the Wokwi Arduino serial monitor. The documentation notes that garbage characters may be printed upon initialization, and the 'How it works' section is marked as TODO:FIXME, indicating incomplete documentation.
results.summary: This Wokwi project is a customizable UART transmitter that sends multiple ASCII characters by storing each character in a column of flip-flops. Characters are set by tying multiplexer inputs to VCC or GND, and more characters can be added by copying and pasting columns. Testing involves setting the baud rate and Wokwi clock to 300, toggling the load/transmit and output-enable switches, and observing the serial output in the Wokwi Arduino serial monitor. The documentation notes that garbage characters may appear at initialization, and the 'How it works' section is marked TODO:FIXME, indicating incomplete documentation.

results.summary_before: This design is an 8-bit R2R digital-to-analog converter (DAC) with a 3.3V output, capable of being driven externally or by an internal sine waveform generator. Silicon tests confirm a smooth sine wave output over the full 3.3V range, with a slight nonlinearity at the mid-code transition. It requires an external multimeter to measure the output voltage. The design uses level shifting drivers to achieve the 3.3V output.

results.summary_before: This design is an audio/visual demo that generates VGA video and PWM audio outputs, forming an 8-part megademo. results.summary_before: Tiny Whisper is a mixed-signal chip that implements a transmitter for the WSPR (Weak Signal Propagation Reporter) protocol in the 3-30 MHz shortwave band. It integrates a digital core containing a CORDIC, a delta-sigma modulator, and local oscillator generation, along with an analog IQ modulator. The design requires external hardware such as an SPI master, UART-to-USB breakout board, and an RF power amplifier with filters and antenna for testing. Documentation is currently incomplete, with references to an external GitHub repository for details.
